title: Feynman's Unbreakable Spaghetti: Why It Never Snaps in Two
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. Bend a stick of dry spaghetti from both ends and it almost never breaks in two; it shatters into three or more pieces. The episode follows this puzzle from Richard Feynman's kitchen experiments to Audoly and Neukirch's two thousand five explanation, which won them an Ig Nobel Prize: the first break sends a bending wave racing back along each fragment, and the wave raises the curvature enough to snap it again. It ends with the two thousand eighteen MIT experiment, which showed that twisting the strand by about two hundred seventy degrees before bending finally lets it break cleanly in two.
